..
Saturday night through Sunday: A cold upper-level low currently 
centered over Central WA will slowly sag to the south/southeast
into Northeastern Oregon over the period. Cooler, and drier 
continental air will be pulled into Inland NW resulting in gusty
north to northeast winds. We are already observing gusty north 
winds through the Okanogan Valley this afternoon. Thee winds 
will continue the night and increase further for Sunday. 
Northeast winds will increase through the Purcell Trench of 
North Idaho and spill into the Columbia Basin through the 
evening and overnight hours. Gusty northeast winds will remain 
in place through the day Sunday. Although temperatures will be 
cooler, the continental air mass will come with much lower 
dewpoints resulting in relative humidities of 25-35%. This 
increases concern for blowing dust across the Central and 
Western Columbia Basin around Moses Lake, Wilbur, and Ritzville 
from Sunday morning through Sunday afternoon. Would not rule out
patchy dust in the Okanogan Valley and over the Waterville 
Plateau but trends will be for the northeast winds to strengthen
over the Basin while the northerly winds decrease Sunday 
afternoon from Omak to Waterville. As such, blowing dust 
advisories have been issued for the areas of greatest 
concern. Will need to closely monitor cams overnight with the
winds increasing and determine if the start time for the blowing
dust advisory needs to be adjusted earlier. 

Moisture spiraling around the periphery of the low will bring a 
threat for convective showers. Afternoon heating will promote 
100-300 J/kg of SB CAPE with a 10-15% chance for an isolated 
lightning strike before sunset. Highest probability for a 
lightning strike is near the Canadian border around Chesaw and 
Northport. Showers in Central and northern WA will decrease 
through the evening with loss of daytime heating. On the 
contrary, showers will increase over the Idaho Panhandle, 
especially along the Montana border. This will fall as snow 
above 4000-4500 feet with light accumulations possible at 
Lookout Pass overnight into Sunday morning with a 20% chance for
picking up an inch of snow. Motorists heading over the pass 
overnight into early Sunday morning should be prepared for 
potentially slick conditions. 

The winds will keep temperatures moderated for most lowlands 
with low probabilities to reach freezing. The greatest risk for
freezing temperatures in the lowlands will be in the sheltered 
valleys of far NE WA and North Idaho where lows will cool 
between 29-33F. 

Monday-Wednesday: The upper-low will begin to slowly drift 
southeast of the region. There will remain residual clouds and 
light showers across the lower Idaho Panhandle and southeastern 
WA Monday morning. Meanwhile, high pressure will begin building 
over Central WA and will eventually work eastward into Idaho by 
Tuesday. A dry air mass, clearing skies, and weakening winds 
will result in chilly overnight lows with many areas close or 
below freezing Monday and Tuesday morning. A hard freeze is 
anticipated across the northern mountain valleys. For the 
valleys still in growing season (Moses Lake Area, Wenatchee 
Area, Lewiston-Clarkston Area, and Pomeroy this will need to be 
monitored closely with strong potential for freeze warnings. At 
this time, Monday morning looks to have borderline temperatures 
with isolated freezing temperatures around Moses Lake and 
Tuesday morning is looking colder. Otherwise, weather impacts 
for this period will be low with the brief ridge of high 
pressure flattening and mainly some passing clouds. There is a 
weak shortwave crossing through on Wednesday that a few models 
generate light showers from but this comes with very confidence 
given the antecedent dry, continental air mass in place. The 
Cascade crest looks to be the most favorable area for light 
rain/snow showers.

Thursday-Sunday: There is good agreement amongst the ensemble 
forecast suites for another ridge to develop Thursday into 
Friday and flatten over the weekend. The pattern remains dry 
with warming temperatures and chilly overnight lows. The 
flattening of the ridge over the weekend will bring the next 
chance for breezy winds and mountain showers. /sb
